title: Of Ants & Aging
description: Presentation given via remote appearAnts at "Curing Aging 2023", on April 22nd 2023 (https://www.curing-aging.com/).

methods.name: Tinbergen's four questions applied to ant and human aging
methods.description: The talk organizes its question of why aging occurs around Tinbergen's 4 Questions, comparing ants (nestmate and colony scales) with humans.
methods.evidence: Why does biological Aging occur? ○Using Tinbergen’s 4 Questions to ask Why aging happens

methods.name: Decayed-house example illustrating four kinds of explanation
methods.description: A worked example explains why a house is decayed in developmental, material, functional and deep-time terms before applying the scheme to aging.
methods.evidence: Because generations of similar houses have been made before, out of materials that are planned to last decades not centuries Next we will use Tinbergen’s 4 Questions to explore Aging.

methods.name: Insulin signaling as a focal example of aging mechanism
methods.description: Mechanism discussion is restricted to insulin signaling, drawing on cited work such as Yan et al. 2022 on long-lived reproductive ant castes.
methods.evidence: This is a large area, here we will just focus on Insulin signaling as an example

methods.name: Kin selection vs. multi-level selection distilled from a prior stream
methods.description: The evolutionary account is limited to kin selection and multi-level selection, presented as a distillation of ActInf PaperStream #001.0.
methods.evidence: Of the many Evolutionary phenomena/perspectives to consider, here we will just discuss Kin Selection (KS) & Multi-Level Selection (MLS)

key_findings: The speaker distinguishes age (clock time elapsed) from aging (a process and embodied outcome linked to species-specific phenotypes and disease/death risk), stating the definition is not normative.
The slides note that some ant species have colonies that do not age, possibly via asexual or intra-nest sexual reproduction.
On the utility of aging, the talk suggests one shared answer for ants and humans may be that there is no specific utility, only an order-vs-disorder tradeoff.
At nestmate scale, the speaker proposes turnover of damaged nestmate bodies may be favorable, favoring aging processes at that scale.
key_findings_evidence: This definition of “aging” is clearly distinct from age, and in no ways is prescriptive or normative.
Some Ant species have colonies that don’t age! Immortal colonies may have asexual reproduction, or intra-nest sexual reproduction
One answer in common might be – there simply is no utility. Life is an Order vs. Disorder tradeoff frontier, and there is no further specific Utility or meaning to Aging
Turnover of damaged nestmate bodies may be favorable (favoring aging processes at nestmate scale)

abstract: A presentation exploring the relationship between social organization and aging in ant colonies, titled 'Of Ants & Aging.' The work examines the paradox of lifespan variation across castes in social insects, where queens can live decades while workers live weeks to months. It connects ant aging biology to broader questions about the evolution of senescence and the role of social structure in shaping longevity.
